title: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A safety committee wants one framework that simultaneously targets preventable harm, evidence-based care, patient preferences, delays, waste, and unequal treatment. Which framework fits all six aims?
questions.explanation: Safe, effective, patient-centered, timely, efficient, and equitable are the six IOM domains of healthcare quality.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient becomes hypoglycemic after a four-hour preop delay caused by scheduling failure, although the eventual treatment is correct. Which quality aim was most directly violated?
questions.explanation: Timely care avoids lengthy waits and delays that could be harmful.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A department routinely opens airway kits that are never used and then discards them. Which quality aim is most directly compromised even if no patient is harmed?
questions.explanation: Efficient care avoids waste of equipment, supplies, ideas, and energy.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Two clinically identical patients request epidural analgesia, but one is denied solely because of insurance status. Which quality aim is violated?
questions.explanation: Equitable care does not vary in quality based on patient characteristics, location, or socioeconomic status.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A cheaper perioperative regimen is chosen despite evidence that it produces worse outcomes than the recommended treatment. Which quality domain is most directly violated?
questions.explanation: Effective care provides evidence- and science-based services to those who could benefit.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A medically reasonable sedative plan is chosen without discussing a patient's clearly stated preference to avoid that medication. Which quality domain is most directly compromised?
questions.explanation: Patient-centered care is respectful and responsive to individual preferences, needs, and values.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Barcode medication scanning is introduced even though it adds a small workflow delay. Which quality aim is the intervention primarily intended to improve?
questions.explanation: The safe domain is the avoidance of harm from care meant to help patients.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A department is tracing the foundation of the modern US patient-safety movement. Which pair of landmark IOM reports should anchor the review?
options: To Err Is Human (1999) and Crossing the Quality Chasm (2001)
Healthy People 2030 and the National Healthcare Quality Report
The Belmont Report and the AANA Code of Ethics
The WHO Surgical Safety Checklist and APSF priorities
questions.explanation: To Err Is Human (IOM, 1999) and Crossing the Quality Chasm (IOM, 2001) are the foundation of the quality domains.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A board asks for the contemporary estimate of annual US deaths attributed to preventable hospital errors. Which range best matches the lecture?
questions.explanation: The original IOM estimate was 44,000–98,000; current data suggest 250,000–400,000 annually.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which range was reported in the original IOM estimate of annual deaths from preventable hospital errors?
questions.explanation: To Err Is Human estimated 44,000–98,000 deaths per year.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: One case involves a mislabeled syringe; another involves choosing the wrong drug because the allergy history was misunderstood. What do the two events have in common?
options: Both are medical errors, whether execution failed or the plan itself was wrong
Both are adverse events only if permanent harm occurred
Both are expected complications of anesthesia
Both are deviations from surgeon preference rather than medical errors
questions.explanation: A medical error is the failure of a planned action to occur as intended, or the use of a wrong plan.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: When medication events are classified broadly, which contributor is expected to account for the largest share even though system conditions often shape the event?
questions.explanation: The majority of medical errors are due to human error, often shaped by system factors.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A chest radiograph is obtained on time, but pneumonia is missed because the image is interpreted incorrectly. Which error category best fits the primary failure?
questions.explanation: Diagnostic errors include delays in diagnosis, misread tests, and failure to order tests.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: The correct antibiotic is clindamycin because of a known allergy, but cefazolin is administered instead. Which error category best describes the event?
questions.explanation: Treatment errors include mistakes in care and medication errors.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A serious allergy is identified correctly in preop, but the information is lost during handoff and the OR team never sees it. Which error category best captures the primary failure?
questions.explanation: Communication breakdowns involve erroneous information between providers or with patients.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: The team knowingly skips the routine anesthesia-machine checkout and a preventable hazard goes undetected. Which error category best fits this failure?
questions.explanation: Preventative failures include missed routine checks and ignoring safety rules.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A 10-fold vasopressor overdose causes only transient hypertension without lasting injury. Which professional obligation remains?
options: Disclose the error to the patient
Disclose only if permanent harm occurred
Report internally but do not inform the patient
Leave disclosure entirely to the surgeon
questions.explanation: Errors must be disclosed, whether or not lasting harm occurred.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Barcode scanning, pharmacy verification, and an independent double-check all exist to stop the same medication error. In the Swiss cheese model, what do these safeguards represent?
questions.explanation: Each slice is a defense layer; harm occurs when holes in several slices line up.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: The barcode scanner is broken, pharmacy staffing is thin, and the independent double-check is skipped. In the Swiss cheese model, what do these weaknesses represent?
questions.explanation: Holes are weaknesses in each defense; when they align, an error reaches the patient.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Wrong-site surgery occurs because small weaknesses in site marking, consent verification, and the time-out align in the same case. Which concept best explains the event?
options: Swiss cheese model with aligned holes across multiple defenses
Failure of a single defense layer
questions.explanation: In the Swiss cheese model, harm reaches the patient when weaknesses in several defensive layers align.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Who developed the Swiss cheese model used to explain how hazards pass through imperfect defense layers?
questions.explanation: The Swiss cheese model of accident causation is attributed to James Reason (1990).
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A wrong-drug event follows an incorrect pharmacy label, skipped double-check, and broken barcode scanner. Which interpretation best matches the Swiss cheese model?
options: Multiple defense failures aligned and allowed the hazard to reach the patient
Any one failed layer would necessarily have caused harm by itself
The patient's condition made the event unavoidable
The event proves layered safeguards are ineffective
questions.explanation: Multiple aligned system flaws allowed the error to reach the patient.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: What should quality assurance and continuous quality improvement programs primarily examine?
options: Processes and systems in both successful and failed care
Punishment of individuals who make errors
Only sentinel events and never successful processes
questions.explanation: QA/CQI programs focus on processes and systems involved in successes and failures.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A department tracks PONV and reintubation rates and reports them externally. What are such quality programs commonly linked to?
questions.explanation: QA and CQI programs are often tied to reimbursement benchmarks and practice standards.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which two items are among the NHQDR core quality areas? (Select 2)
questions.explanation: The six graded areas are patient safety, person-centered care, care coordination, effective treatment, healthy living, and care affordability.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A health system expands vaccination clinics and smoking-cessation programs. Which NHQDR core area is being addressed?
questions.explanation: Healthy living covers wellness promotion and preventive care.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which NHQDR core area focuses on avoiding preventable errors and hospital-acquired infections?
questions.explanation: Patient safety includes healthcare quality, protection from avoidable errors, and HAIs.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A hospital's postoperative sepsis rate is 12.5 per 1,000 operations. If it improves by the same 31.9% reported nationally, approximately what rate would remain?
questions.explanation: A 31.9% drop removes about 4.0 cases: 12.5 × 0.681 ≈ 8.5 per 1,000.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Opioid prescribing restrictions were implemented, yet overdose deaths continued to rise. Which trend best explains why prescription limits alone had only modest impact?
options: A growing share of deaths involved synthetic opioids such as illicit fentanyl
Benzodiazepines became the leading cause of overdose death
Natural opioids caused most recent deaths
questions.explanation: Recent opioid mortality is driven largely by synthetic opioids, which prescribing limits do not address.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A pediatric anesthesia practice is addressing rising anxiety and depression among adolescents. Which group is described as having the most limited access to mental-health treatment?
questions.explanation: Adolescent mental health need has grown, with access especially limited among low-income and Hispanic youths.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which kidney-failure treatment is preferred but remains accessible to relatively few patients according to the cited report?
questions.explanation: Transplantation offers better quality of life and life expectancy but is accessible to relatively few.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which insurance group was reported to experience a higher burden of healthcare costs in the cited findings?
options: People with Medicare rather than private insurance
questions.explanation: More Americans, particularly those with private insurance, report a higher cost burden.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which 2021 life-expectancy comparison best reflects the cited US-versus-peer-nation data?
options: US 76.1 years versus 82.4 years in similar nations
US 82.4 years versus 76.1 years in similar nations
US 70.2 years versus 78.5 years in similar nations
US 79.0 years versus 80.0 years in similar nations
questions.explanation: In 2021, US life expectancy lagged at 76.1 years versus 82.4 years in comparable nations.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which four causes contribute importantly to premature US mortality compared with peer nations? (Select 4)
questions.explanation: Important causes of premature death include unintentional injury, heart disease, liver disease, and suicide.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which condition remains the leading cause of death in the United States and therefore a major perioperative risk focus?
questions.explanation: Heart disease leads, followed by cancer and unintentional injury.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Where does unintentional injury rank among leading US causes of death in the cited material?
questions.explanation: The order is heart disease, cancer, then unintentional injury, followed by stroke and chronic lung disease.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Two patients receive equivalent medical care, but one has unstable housing and no transportation and experiences worse outcomes. What principle does this illustrate?
options: Social determinants can influence outcomes more strongly than healthcare delivery alone
Social determinants have little effect compared with clinical care
Social determinants matter only in pediatrics
questions.explanation: Evidence shows SDOH have a stronger influence on outcomes than healthcare delivery itself.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which four items are Healthy People 2030 social-determinants-of-health domains? (Select 4)
questions.explanation: The five domains are economic stability, education, healthcare access, neighborhood/built environment, and social/community context.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient misses preop testing because transportation is unaffordable. Which social-determinant domain is most directly involved?
questions.explanation: Financial limits affecting access relate to economic stability.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient lives in an area without a pharmacy and with unsafe walking routes. Which social-determinant domain best fits?
questions.explanation: The physical environment falls under neighborhood and built environment.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient cannot understand discharge instructions because of low health literacy. Which social-determinant domain is most directly involved?
questions.explanation: Health literacy connects to education access and quality.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient scheduled for outpatient surgery lives alone, lacks transportation, and cannot afford medications. When should these barriers be identified?
options: During care coordination before they disrupt the plan
Only if the patient is uninsured
questions.explanation: SDOH should be assessed and prioritized during care coordination so the plan can address them early.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: An anesthesia department standardizes evidence-based protocols across both its main hospital and rural satellite. Which equity priority does this most directly support?
options: High-quality perioperative care for all populations
questions.explanation: The ASA's first equity priority is high-quality perioperative care for all populations.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: According to the cited disparity data, Black, American Indian, and Alaska Native patients received lower-quality care than White patients for approximately what proportion of measures?
questions.explanation: They received lower quality care for 40% of quality measures (AHRQ, 2021).
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which two postoperative safety measures were cited as showing worse care for Black adults? (Select 2)
questions.explanation: Worse care for Black adults included postoperative sepsis and pulmonary embolism, along with physiologic or metabolic derangements and AKI.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: An audit finds Black and Hispanic women with similar labor pain scores receive epidural analgesia less often than White women. What disparity does this demonstrate?
options: Lower access to epidural labor analgesia among minority women
Higher epidural-request rates among minority women
Lower pain severity among minority women
questions.explanation: Minority women are less likely to receive epidural labor analgesia, which affects later cesarean anesthesia.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Why can lower epidural use during labor matter when an emergency cesarean becomes necessary?
options: Without a functioning neuraxial catheter, general anesthesia may be required, adding risk and delaying maternal-newborn interaction
General anesthesia is safer than neuraxial anesthesia for cesarean delivery
questions.explanation: GA for cesarean carries higher airway and aspiration risk and delays bonding, so epidural access matters.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: How much higher is pregnancy-related mortality reported to be among minority women in the cited material?
questions.explanation: Racial and ethnic minority women are two to three times more likely to die from pregnancy-related causes.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A program ensures patients with sickle cell disease receive timely and adequate analgesia in the ED and OR. Which ASA equity priority does this most directly address?
options: High-quality perioperative care for all populations
questions.explanation: The ASA's third equity priority is access to pain management.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Black patients with long-bone fractures receive less analgesia than White patients with comparable injuries. Which factor is cited as contributing to this disparity?
options: False clinician beliefs about biological differences in pain
True race-based biological differences in pain perception
questions.explanation: Clinicians' false beliefs about racial biological differences contribute to disparities in pain treatment.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient's postoperative pain is repeatedly undertreated. Which long-term consequences can follow? (Select 3)
questions.explanation: Undertreated pain can lead to disability, drug dependence, and even mortality.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient with frequent sickle cell crises keeps receiving fragmented ED care. Which resource does the ASA highlight for integrated pain care?
questions.explanation: The ASA highlights sickle cell centers for integrated pain care.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: An ED audit of children with appendicitis and moderate to severe pain finds a racial gap in treatment. What did a 2015 JAMA study show?
options: Black children were less likely to receive analgesia
White children were less likely to receive analgesia
questions.explanation: Black children with appendicitis were less likely to receive analgesia for moderate or severe pain.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A rural hospital without pediatric anesthesiologists cares for a 2-year-old with an upper respiratory infection for ear tubes. Why are pediatric patients an equity priority?
options: Higher respiratory risk and less access to pediatric specialists
Children have higher rates of PONV
questions.explanation: Children have higher perioperative respiratory risk, and many lack access to pediatric anesthesia specialists.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Of 1,000 uninsured patients seen in a county clinic, about how many would you expect to be from minority groups?
questions.explanation: Minorities make up over half of the uninsured population.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A registry review finds that patients with low income or no insurance received fewer antiemetics despite similar PONV risk. Which study found this?
questions.explanation: The Andreae (2018) registry linked insurance status and income to antiemetic receipt.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Besides lack of insurance, which factors limit access to quality care? (Select 4)
questions.explanation: Other factors include no paid sick leave, low health literacy, language barriers, and distrust.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which APSF clinician-level strategies mitigate disparities? (Select 2)
options: Tie department bonuses to equity metrics
Provide financial incentives for equity measures
Create a culture of equity systemwide
questions.explanation: Clinician-level strategies are personal: recognizing bias and pursuing education. Financial incentives, governance, and culture are system-level strategies.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which APSF strategies are system-level? (Select 3)
options: Financial incentives tied to equity measures
Engage in community outreach as an individual
questions.explanation: System-level strategies involve culture, training, research, incentives, and governance.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA notices she spends less time explaining risks to non-English-speaking patients and wants to change. Which AANA recommended action applies?
options: Be consciously aware of one's own implicit bias
Avoid interacting with patients from other cultures
Rely on intuition rather than reflection
questions.explanation: The AANA recommends that CRNAs be consciously aware of their implicit bias.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA completes a cultural sensitivity module and says, "Now I'm culturally competent." How does the AANA frame cultural humility?
options: As a requirement for cultural competency certification
questions.explanation: The AANA embraces cultural humility as a life-long process of learning and self-reflection.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which AANA recommendations address the workforce? (Select 2)
options: Encourage diverse students to consider nurse anesthesiology
Incorporate cultural competency training into practice
Limit outcomes data to hospital leadership
Limit recruitment to a single background
questions.explanation: The AANA recommends recruiting diverse students and building cultural competency into practice, along with anti-racist policies and shared outcomes data.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA arranges an interpreter for a Spanish-speaking patient before consent. Which AANA recommendation does this follow?
options: Accommodate literacy needs and linguistic barriers
Encourage diverse students to join the profession
Develop anti-discrimination policy at the facility
questions.explanation: Accommodating literacy and language barriers is an AANA recommendation.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which are the four ethical pillars? (Select 4)
questions.explanation: The four pillars are beneficence, non-maleficence, autonomy, and justice.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA places a nerve block to reduce opioid use and speed recovery for a patient. Which ethical pillar does this action reflect?
questions.explanation: Beneficence is the duty to do good for the patient.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA declines to give a drug to which the patient had a prior reaction, choosing a safer alternative. Which ethical pillar does this reflect?
questions.explanation: Non-maleficence is the duty to avoid harm.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A competent Jehovah's Witness refuses blood products after a full discussion. The CRNA respects the refusal. Which pillar is MOST upheld?
questions.explanation: Autonomy respects the patient's right to self-determination.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA gives the same attention and analgesic options to an uninsured patient as to a VIP. Which pillar is upheld?
questions.explanation: Justice is treating all people equally and equitably.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA declines to give a sedative that would benefit the surgeon's workflow but raise the patient's aspiration risk. Which pillar is upheld?
questions.explanation: Avoiding harm to the patient reflects non-maleficence.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA places a regional block to reduce opioid use and improve recovery. Which pillar does this primarily reflect?
questions.explanation: Acting to benefit the patient reflects beneficence.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient wants a spinal, but the CRNA insists on GA because it is "easier" without discussing risks. Which pillar is MOST violated?
questions.explanation: Overriding an informed patient's choice without discussion violates autonomy.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A department schedules uninsured patients last every day, causing longer NPO times and delays. Which pillar is violated?
questions.explanation: Unequal treatment based on insurance violates justice.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which topics does the AANA Code of Ethics address? (Select 2)
options: Responsibility to maximize operating room efficiency
Responsibility to the hospital's financial goals
questions.explanation: The Code covers responsibility to patients and as a professional, plus research, business practice, and society.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA delays a case because the patient's dignity is being compromised by leaving her uncovered during positioning. Which core principle of the Code applies?
options: Patients first: safety, comfort, and dignity
questions.explanation: The core principle of patients first emphasizes safety, comfort, and dignity.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA reports an unsafe practice by a colleague to protect patients. Which core principle is this?
questions.explanation: Advocacy means speaking up for patient rights and unsafe practices.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA completes annual simulation and continuing education. Which core principle is this?
questions.explanation: Skill maintenance means lifelong learning and maintaining expertise.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA identifies and corrects bias in how she assesses pain in different groups. Which core principle is this?
questions.explanation: Fairness includes treating people equally and actively fixing biases.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which core principle helps patients make the best, safest choices for their own care?
questions.explanation: Informed consent helps patients make the best and safest choices.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A senior CRNA mentors students, maintains certification, and models professional behavior. Which responsibility in the Code does this reflect?
questions.explanation: Responsibility as a professional covers competence, leadership, and role modeling.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient experience committee builds its survey around the dimensions of patient-centered care. How many dimensions should it include?
questions.explanation: Patient-centered care has eight dimensions.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which are dimensions of patient-centered care? (Select 4)
questions.explanation: Dimensions include preferences, emotional support, comfort, information, continuity, coordination, family, and access.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA explains each step of induction to an anxious patient and answers questions. Which dimension is MOST reflected?
options: Access to care and scheduling convenience
questions.explanation: Explaining and educating reflects information, communication, and education.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA gives a thorough handoff to PACU including pain plan and concerns. Which dimension is reflected?
questions.explanation: Handoffs support continuity and transition.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA warms the patient and pads pressure points. Which dimension is reflected?
questions.explanation: Physical comfort includes warmth and positioning.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA lets a child's parent stay for mask induction. Which dimension is reflected?
options: Access to care through transportation help
questions.explanation: Involving family is a patient-centered dimension.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which informed consent topics does the AANA guidance address? (Select 4)
questions.explanation: Consent guidance covers surgical and anesthesia consent, timing, emergencies, withheld information, literacy, and special populations.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which patients need special attention during the anesthesia consent process? (Select 3)
options: A patient with limited English proficiency
A healthy adult having a repeat procedure
questions.explanation: Special consent populations include obstetric patients, cognitively impaired patients, and those with limited English proficiency.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient with limited English proficiency is scheduled for surgery. What is the BEST way to obtain consent?
options: Ask a family member to translate quickly
Have the patient sign without explanation
questions.explanation: Communication and health literacy are key consent considerations; use qualified interpreters.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A surgery center wants a streamlined consent form that skips some state-required elements. Which requirements must consent follow?
options: Federal, state, local, facility, and accreditation requirements
Facility policy, which can modify state requirements
Hospital policy but not state law
questions.explanation: Consent processes must meet all federal, state, local, facility, and accreditation requirements.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient in labor is in severe pain when asked to consent for an epidural. What consent consideration applies?
options: Special population considerations for obstetric consent
Consent is not needed during labor
Her partner must consent during active labor
Consent must be delayed until after delivery
questions.explanation: Obstetrics is a special population with specific consent considerations.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient with dementia is scheduled for hip surgery. What consent consideration applies?
options: Assess capacity and involve a legal surrogate if needed
Obtain consent from the patient without assessment
Have the surgeon sign on her behalf
Let the surgeon consent for anesthesia
questions.explanation: Cognitively impaired patients require capacity assessment and surrogate consent when needed.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: In an emergency with an unconscious patient and no surrogate, how is consent addressed?
options: Emergency provisions per law and policy
Two-physician consent is required before any care
The patient must be woken to consent
Anesthesia is withheld until consent is obtained
questions.explanation: Consent guidance includes emergency situations governed by law and policy.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A hospital trains staff to adjust communication, respect beliefs, and change policies to serve diverse patients. What does this describe?
options: Knowing the religious beliefs of every patient
Providing identical care to every patient
Providing care in the patient's native language at all times
questions.explanation: Cultural competence is a set of attitudes, skills, behaviors, and policies that let clinicians work effectively across cultures.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which are risks of failing at cultural competence? (Select 2)
options: Patients fail to seek or trust care
questions.explanation: Failing at cultural competence reduces trust and causes miscommunication, missed services, and liability.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A department trains staff to adapt communication to patients' beliefs and use interpreters. What outcomes is this culturally competent care meant to produce?
questions.explanation: Culturally competent care builds trust, improves safety, and reduces disparities.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient's culture discourages eye contact, and the CRNA adjusts communication style. What does this show?
options: Recognition of diverse health-related beliefs and values
Paternalism in care decisions for the patient
Avoidance of patient involvement in cultural decisions
questions.explanation: Responding to cultural values is part of cultural competence.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: You are designing a study comparing two antiemetic regimens. Which ethical principles must the protocol uphold? (Select 3)
questions.explanation: Research upholds autonomy, beneficence, and justice.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which protections does research ethics promote? (Select 4)
options: The right to withdraw at any time
questions.explanation: Research ethics promotes voluntary participation, confidentiality, and privacy.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA wants to study a new antiemetic regimen in patients. Which body must approve and oversee the study?
questions.explanation: An IRB provides approval and oversight for human research.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: An IRB reviews your proposed perioperative study. Which groups require added protections as vulnerable populations? (Select 4)
questions.explanation: Vulnerable research populations include pregnant women and fetuses, minors, prisoners, and those unable to consent.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A researcher wants to enroll ICU patients who are sedated and cannot consent. What consideration applies?
options: They are vulnerable and need special protections
They can be enrolled without consent
They can be enrolled with deferred consent in any study
Consent is not needed for minimal risk studies
questions.explanation: Those who lack ability to consent require additional protections.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A research consent form describes the study drug but omits possible side effects. What is missing?
questions.explanation: Research consent must clearly describe anticipated risks and benefits.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA collects outcome data on disparities with IRB approval and de-identified data. Which ethical principle is protected?
options: Paternalism in how results are reported
questions.explanation: De-identification protects confidentiality and privacy.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which are APSF perioperative safety priorities (2021)? (Select 2)
questions.explanation: APSF priorities include NORA safety and perioperative delirium and brain health, along with culture of safety, medication safety, burnout, and distractions.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient's allergy was not passed on during an OR-to-PACU handoff, and she received the allergen. Which APSF priority addresses this?
questions.explanation: Handoff errors fall under patient-related communication and transitions of care.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During a stable 4-hour case, a CRNA notices a subtle 6 mmHg ETCO2 rise and investigates. Which concept does this illustrate?
options: Vigilance: readiness to detect and respond to small, random changes
Constant awareness of the surgeon's timeline
questions.explanation: Vigilance is readiness to detect and respond to small changes that occur at random intervals.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During a case, a CRNA recalls the patient's preop BP, notes the current trend, and predicts hypotension when the surgeon clamps the aorta. What does this describe?
options: Situational awareness across past, present, and future
questions.explanation: Situational awareness includes past, present, and projected future status.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA reviews the patient's history of difficult airway, watches current monitors, and prepares for possible bronchospasm. Which concept is this?
options: Fixation error on one airway problem
questions.explanation: Perceiving past, present, and projecting future risk is situational awareness.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A provider relies on automated alarms and stops actively scanning the monitors during a long case. What risk does automation pose?
options: A passive role with fatigue and less vigilance
questions.explanation: Automation can shift providers into a passive role, reducing vigilance.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Loud music in the OR masks the SpO2 tone, and desaturation goes unnoticed. What type of distraction is this?
questions.explanation: Loud music that masks alarms is an auditory disruption.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA looks at a phone during maintenance. Which type of distraction is this?
questions.explanation: Devices that divert the eyes are visual distractions.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA is preparing drugs for the next case while monitoring the current patient. Which type of distraction is this?
questions.explanation: Multitasking and preparing for other patients increase cognitive load.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which strategies reduce distractions? (Select 4)
options: Minimize noise during induction and emergence
Allow personal device use during induction
Allow phones for clinical reference only
questions.explanation: Strategies include noise limits, alarm protocols, focused time-outs, and OR traffic control.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During induction, the circulator starts asking about lunch orders. Which rule should apply?
options: The sterile OR rule: safety-related communication only
questions.explanation: The sterile OR rule limits communication to safety-related topics during critical periods.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During induction, the surgeon wants to discuss a weekend plan. What should the CRNA do?
options: Politely defer non-case conversation until after induction
Ask the circulator to answer the surgeon for you
Stop induction to finish the conversation first
questions.explanation: Minimize distractions during critical periods like induction.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which policies help reduce distractions? (Select 3)
options: Unlimited device use in the OR
Leaving time-out format to each team
questions.explanation: Policies include device rules, checklists, and time-out adherence.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: After a 16-hour shift, a CRNA feels overwhelmingly tired and miscalculates a drug dose. How does the AANA define fatigue?
options: Normal tiredness at the end of a shift
questions.explanation: The AANA defines fatigue as overwhelming tiredness with impaired physical or cognitive function.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which are signs of fatigue? (Select 2)
questions.explanation: Fatigue causes diminished reflexes and impaired decision-making, along with memory lapses and repeated rechecking of finished tasks.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA has been awake for 26 hours after a busy call shift. What effects should be expected? (Select 3)
questions.explanation: Prolonged wakefulness impairs alertness, performance, cognition, and vigilance.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: What steps are recommended to reduce fatigue risk? (Select 5)
options: Allow scheduled breaks during long cases
questions.explanation: Minimize consecutive hours, promote sleep and wellness, and address threats to safety.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA after a 24-hour shift keeps rechecking a drug label and misses a falling BP. What does this reflect?
questions.explanation: Multiple rechecks and missed changes are signs of fatigue.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which are links in the chain of infection? (Select 3)
questions.explanation: The chain includes infectious agent, reservoir, exit, transmission, entry, and susceptible host.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA cleans her hands and wears gloves before touching the patient's IV. Which link in the chain of infection does this break?
questions.explanation: Hand hygiene and PPE break the transmission link.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient on chemotherapy with an ANC of 300 is scheduled for a port placement. Which chain of infection link does he represent?
questions.explanation: An immunocompromised patient is a susceptible host at high risk of infection.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which WHO moment of hand hygiene occurs before touching a patient?
questions.explanation: Moment 1 is before touching a patient.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA is about to place an arterial line. Which WHO hand hygiene moment applies right before insertion?
options: Moment 2: before a clean or aseptic procedure
questions.explanation: Moment 2 is before a clean or aseptic procedure.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which WHO moment occurs after body fluid exposure risk?
questions.explanation: Moment 3 is after body fluid exposure risk.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which WHO moment occurs after touching a patient?
questions.explanation: Moment 4 is after touching a patient.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which WHO moment occurs after touching patient surroundings?
questions.explanation: Moment 5 is after touching patient surroundings.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA intubates and then touches the anesthesia cart without changing gloves. Which zone rule is violated?
options: Contaminating a clean zone after touching a dirty zone
Wearing gloves for all tasks at the workstation
questions.explanation: Clean hands or change gloves after dirty (red) zone contact before touching clean (green) zones.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: You touch the clean drug drawer, then a clean syringe on the workstation. Both are green zones. Is hand hygiene required between them?
options: No, between green zones it is not required
questions.explanation: Hand hygiene is not required between green (clean) zone contacts.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: After which actions should hands be cleaned per the workstation slide? (Select 2)
options: Touching a green zone after another green zone
questions.explanation: Clean hands after touching a cellphone or picking items off the floor, and after airway manipulation.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: How often does APSF recommend hand hygiene during anesthesia care?
questions.explanation: APSF recommends hand hygiene at least 8 times per hour.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Your department wants to lower its perioperative infection rates. Which strategies are supported? (Select 4)
questions.explanation: Perioperative infection strategies include decolonization, hand hygiene, vascular access care, and environmental cleaning.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: An SSI occurs 20 days after an appendectomy. Does it qualify as an SSI?
options: No, SSIs are counted within 7 days
No, SSIs require an implant to count
Yes, but it counts if he is readmitted
questions.explanation: SSIs include infections within 30 days postop.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: An infection develops 70 days after a total knee replacement. Does it qualify as an SSI?
options: Yes, within 90 days with prosthetic implant
No, because it is an implant
Yes, but it counts if the infection is superficial
questions.explanation: SSIs involving prosthetic implants count up to 90 days.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient develops an SSI after a hip replacement. How does CMS treat this?
questions.explanation: CMS classifies SSIs as preventable and does not reimburse them.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Incision is planned for 0800. When should cefazolin be given?
questions.explanation: Most prophylactic antibiotics should be given within 60 minutes before incision.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Incision is planned for 0900. A patient with MRSA needs vancomycin. When can the infusion start?
questions.explanation: Vancomycin and fluoroquinolones may start up to 120 minutes before incision.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A colectomy patient's temperature is 96.2 °F at the end of the case. What normothermia target supports SSI prevention?
questions.explanation: Maintaining normothermia, typically above 97 °F, reduces surgical site infection.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A diabetic patient's intraoperative glucose is 228 mg/dL during a colectomy. What glucose target supports SSI prevention?
questions.explanation: Glycemic control below 180 mg/dL reduces surgical site infection.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: For a healthy patient having a colectomy, a protocol suggests higher intraoperative oxygen to reduce SSIs. What FiO2 does some evidence support?
options: Room air to limit oxidative stress
questions.explanation: Some evidence supports FiO2 above 0.8 to lower SSI risk.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During a colectomy, a patient receives 6 L of crystalloid and develops bowel edema. Which fluid goal supports SSI prevention?
questions.explanation: Normovolemia (euvolemia) supports SSI prevention.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which are SSI prevention strategies? (Select 5)
questions.explanation: Prevention includes antibiotics, normothermia, glucose control, oxygenation, and normovolemia.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During intubation of a patient with influenza, fine droplets and droplet nuclei are released. How does the WHO define this procedure?
questions.explanation: An AGP is a procedure that produces aerosols, including droplet nuclei.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which PPE is recommended for AGPs? (Select 2)
options: Surgical cap and shoe covers only
questions.explanation: PPE for AGPs includes gloves, long-sleeved gowns, eye protection, and a surgical or N95 mask.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which procedures carry higher infection transmission risk based on evidence? (Select 3)
questions.explanation: Higher-risk AGPs include intubation, NIV/CPAP, tracheostomy, and manual ventilation.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During a respiratory virus surge, which procedures require airborne precautions as aerosol-generating? (Select 4)
questions.explanation: AGPs include extubation, open suctioning, bronchoscopy, airway surgery, HFNO, and upper GI endoscopy.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which AGPs have unclear risk? (Select 3)
questions.explanation: Unclear-risk AGPs include compressions, defibrillation, NG tubes, NIV mask adjustment, nebulizers, and ventilator disconnection.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA is about to extubate a patient with a respiratory infection. Which PPE is appropriate?
options: Gloves, gown, eye protection, and a surgical or N95 mask
Gloves, since extubation is brief and low risk
questions.explanation: Extubation is an AGP requiring full PPE.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient with a suspected respiratory infection is scheduled for several procedures. Which one is aerosol-generating?
questions.explanation: Upper GI endoscopy is an aerosol-generating procedure; colonoscopy is not.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During an infectious outbreak, which surgical technique generates aerosols and requires added precautions?
options: Surgery with high-speed devices such as drills
questions.explanation: Surgery using high-speed devices is an aerosol-generating procedure.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During a crisis, a CRNA intubates quickly but fails to call for help or share the plan with the team. Which skill set was lacking?
options: Non-technical skills: cognitive, social, and personal skills
questions.explanation: Non-technical skills are cognitive, social, and personal resource skills that complement technical skills for safe performance.
questions.topic: Crisis resource management and non-technical skills
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which are non-technical skills? (Select 4)
questions.explanation: NTS include situational awareness, decision making, teamwork, leadership, and stress/fatigue management.
questions.topic: Crisis resource management and non-technical skills
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: What roles do non-technical skills play in crisis prevention? (Select 3)
questions.explanation: NTS help minimize errors, identify crises early, initiate interventions, and support communication and leadership.
questions.topic: Crisis resource management and non-technical skills
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During a crisis, a CRNA says "Give epinephrine 1 mg IV," and the nurse replies "Epinephrine 1 mg IV given." Which CRM principle is this?
questions.explanation: Clear, closed-loop communication is a core CRM principle.
questions.topic: Crisis resource management and non-technical skills
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which errors have resulted from CRM communication breakdowns? (Select 2)
questions.explanation: Communication breakdowns have caused retained foreign objects and wrong-sided nerve blocks, as well as medication errors.
questions.topic: Crisis resource management and non-technical skills
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During a code, the CRNA says, "I'm leading; you do compressions, you manage drugs, you record." Which CRM principle is this?
questions.explanation: CRM leadership involves clear articulation and role designation.
questions.topic: Crisis resource management and non-technical skills
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During a massive hemorrhage, a CRNA anticipates the need for blood products and calls for the rapid infuser before BP falls. Which CRM principle is this?
questions.explanation: Situational awareness includes monitoring, anticipating problems, and allocating resources.
questions.topic: Crisis resource management and non-technical skills
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During an MH crisis, the team leader asks members for input, then quickly decides to give dantrolene. Which CRM principle is this?
questions.explanation: Dynamic decision making means quick, informed decisions with input from team members.
questions.topic: Crisis resource management and non-technical skills
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During a CRM debrief, the team notes the CRNA anticipated the hemorrhage, planned ahead, and kept attention on the patient. Which CRM element is this?
questions.explanation: In the CRM wheel, A stands for awareness, anticipation, planning, and attention.
questions.topic: Crisis resource management and non-technical skills
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During a code, a CRNA steps out of the airway role to run medications because that is what the team needs. Which CRM element does this show?
options: Behavioral flexibility: building the team and filling the needed role
Briefing the plan before the procedure
questions.explanation: In the CRM wheel, B stands for behavioral flexibility, building the team, and being in the needed role.
questions.topic: Crisis resource management and non-technical skills
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During an MH crisis, the CRNA calls for help and has a nurse read the MH cognitive aid aloud. Which CRM element is this?
options: Communication: cognitive aids and calling for help
questions.explanation: In the CRM wheel, C stands for communication, cognitive aids, and calling for help.
questions.topic: Crisis resource management and non-technical skills
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During a massive hemorrhage, the CRNA decides what to treat first and assigns blood, lines, and labs to different team members. Which CRM element is this?
options: Dynamic prioritization: decisions and workload distribution
questions.explanation: In the CRM wheel, D stands for dynamic prioritization, decision making, and distribution of workload.
questions.topic: Crisis resource management and non-technical skills
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: After a near miss, the team reviews what went wrong and how the room setup contributed. Which CRM element does this reflect?
options: Exposure for a full patient exam
questions.explanation: In the CRM wheel, E stands for evaluation, error wisdom, and environment.
questions.topic: Crisis resource management and non-technical skills
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During a crisis, the CRNA asks the circulator to bring the difficult airway cart and assigns a colleague to call for help. Which CRM element is demonstrated?
options: Fixation on a single diagnosis during the event
questions.explanation: Distributing tasks is part of dynamic prioritization.
questions.topic: Crisis resource management and non-technical skills
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA calls for help early during unexpected hypoxemia. Which CRM element does this reflect?
options: Behavioral flexibility: being in needed role
questions.explanation: Calling for help is part of the communication component.
questions.topic: Crisis resource management and non-technical skills
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA reviews what went wrong after an event to improve future care. Which CRM element is this?
questions.explanation: Evaluation includes error wisdom and learning from events.
questions.topic: Crisis resource management and non-technical skills
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During hypotension, a CRNA keeps giving phenylephrine for "vasodilation from propofol" and ignores the rising PIP and absent breath sounds on one side. What error is this?
questions.explanation: Fixation errors lock in one explanation and ignore new information, here a tension pneumothorax.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: "The hypotension must be related to the anesthetic," while hemorrhage is ignored. Which fixation error is this?
options: Cognitive tunnel vision ("this and only this")
questions.explanation: Tunnel vision focuses on one cause and ignores others.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: "It can't be anaphylaxis. That reaction is quite rare." Which fixation error is this?
questions.explanation: Avoidance error dismisses a diagnosis because it seems unlikely.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: "It's just the surgeon leaning on the BP cuff; I'm sure it's fine." Which fixation error is this?
questions.explanation: Artifact error assumes an abnormal reading is artifact.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which strategies reduce fixation errors? (Select 3)
questions.explanation: Cognitive aids, breaks, teamwork, and simulation reduce fixation errors.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During an MH crisis, a nurse reads the MH checklist aloud step by step. What tool is being used?
questions.explanation: Cognitive aids such as checklists guide providers during high-stress events.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which are examples of cognitive aids? (Select 5)
questions.explanation: Examples include the Stanford manual, WHO checklist, MH carts, and difficult airway algorithm.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: How do cognitive aids help during crises? (Select 3)
options: Replace the need for a team leader
questions.explanation: Cognitive aids reduce errors, omissions, and variability.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During MH, the team uses the MH cart's step-by-step card. What is this an example of?
questions.explanation: MH carts with instructions are cognitive aids.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During a difficult airway, the team follows the difficult airway algorithm. What is this?
questions.explanation: The difficult airway algorithm is a cognitive aid.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which cognitive aid supports the safety time-out before incision?
questions.explanation: The WHO Surgical Safety Checklist supports the time-out.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA draws up phenylephrine and ephedrine in identical syringes and gives the wrong one. After the event, the department adds color-coded labels and a barcode scanner. What is this response?
options: A punitive response to individual error
An equity intervention for underserved groups
questions.explanation: QI focuses on processes and systems to prevent recurrence.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: After a wrong-site block, the review looks at the time-out process, site marking, and staffing instead of just blaming the provider. What approach is this?
options: Continuous quality improvement focused on systems
Blame-based error management for the provider
questions.explanation: CQI examines processes and systems in both successes and failures.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A wrong-site surgery is reported as a sentinel event. What do QA programs focus on?
options: Processes and systems that allowed the event
Hiding the event to protect reputation
Identifying the individual responsible for discipline
questions.explanation: QA programs review processes and systems, including sentinel events.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA discovers she gave a double dose of ondansetron. The patient has no harm. What should she do?
options: Say nothing because there was no harm
Chart that the dose was correct
questions.explanation: The lecture states errors must be disclosed.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient's postoperative delirium is not recognized for a day because no one screened for it. Which error type is MOST applicable?
options: Diagnostic error (delay in finding the diagnosis)
Communication breakdown between providers and staff
questions.explanation: Delays in diagnosis are diagnostic errors.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A PACU nurse was told the patient received morphine when it was actually hydromorphone, leading to overdosing. Which error type is this?
options: Diagnostic error in identifying the drug
questions.explanation: Erroneous information between providers is a communication breakdown.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A hospital stops routine anesthesia machine maintenance to cut costs, and a vaporizer fails. Which error type is this?
questions.explanation: Ignoring routine safety checks is a preventative failure.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which quality domain would a new ERAS protocol with evidence-based multimodal analgesia MOST support?
questions.explanation: Evidence-based care supports the effective domain.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A hospital tracks antiemetic administration by insurance status to find gaps. Which quality domain does this support?
questions.explanation: Measuring differences by patient characteristics supports equity.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A department reduces delays for emergent C-sections by staffing an in-house anesthesia team. Which domain is MOST improved?
questions.explanation: Reducing harmful delays improves timeliness.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA adapts the anesthetic to the patient's religious beliefs after discussion. Which domain is MOST reflected?
options: Efficient, since the discussion took extra time
questions.explanation: Respecting individual values reflects patient-centered care.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A hospital introduces a bundle that lowers postoperative infections. Which NHQDR core area is improved?
questions.explanation: HAIs fall under patient safety.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: An interdisciplinary team uses a shared plan for a complex patient across units. Which NHQDR core area is this?
questions.explanation: Coordinated interdisciplinary efforts are care coordination.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A clinic runs smoking cessation classes before elective surgery. Which NHQDR core area is this?
questions.explanation: Wellness promotion and prevention are healthy living.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A hospital reduces out-of-pocket costs for surgical patients. Which NHQDR core area is this?
questions.explanation: Reducing costs falls under care affordability.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A Black woman in labor is offered GA for a non-urgent cesarean while an epidural could have been used. Which equity concern does this reflect?
options: Disparity in anesthetic technique and bonding
An appropriate choice given her labor progress
Improved maternal safety from a secured airway
A cost-saving measure for the hospital
questions.explanation: Black women are more likely to receive GA, increasing risk and reducing bonding.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A Hispanic adolescent needs mental health services but cannot access them. Which 2023 finding does this reflect?
options: Limited access to adolescent mental health care
Declining need for mental health services
questions.explanation: The 2023 report notes limited access for low-income and Hispanic youth.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient with ESRD on dialysis asks about transplant but lacks access. Which 2023 finding does this reflect?
options: Few Americans have access to preferred transplant care
Dialysis outcomes have improved enough to replace transplant
Kidney disease is not a leading cause of death in the US
questions.explanation: Transplant is preferred but relatively few have access.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A clinician gives a Black patient less opioid than a white patient with the same fracture because "they tolerate pain better." What does this represent?
options: False beliefs that contribute to pain disparities
The standard of care for pain management
questions.explanation: False beliefs about biological differences in pain contribute to racial disparities in treatment.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A sickle cell patient with chronic pain lacks integrated pain care. Which ASA priority applies?
questions.explanation: The ASA supports sickle cell centers to improve chronic pain access.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A child from a minority background receives less analgesia for severe pain in the ED. Which ASA priority applies?
questions.explanation: The pediatric priority includes disparities in analgesia.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: An uninsured patient delays surgery until an emergency occurs. Which ASA priority applies?
options: Pain management access for chronic pain
questions.explanation: Uninsured adults are less likely to receive critical and preventive services.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient works hourly without paid sick leave and misses two preop testing appointments. Which barrier is affecting access?
questions.explanation: Lack of paid sick leave limits access to care and is an equity barrier.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient distrusts the healthcare system due to past discrimination. Which barrier is this?
options: Long-standing distrust of the healthcare system
Low health literacy that prevents understanding
questions.explanation: Distrust is listed as a factor limiting quality care.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A department creates a health equity training program for all staff. Which APSF level is this?
questions.explanation: Providing health equity training is a system-level strategy.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA volunteers at a community health fair to address disparities. Which APSF level is this?
questions.explanation: Community outreach is a clinician-level strategy.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA seeks CE courses on disparities in anesthesia care. Which APSF level is this?
questions.explanation: Participating in education is clinician-level.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A hospital ties bonuses to closing disparities in PONV prophylaxis. Which APSF level is this?
questions.explanation: Financial incentives for equity are system-level.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA collects outcomes by race and ethnicity for QI with permission. Which AANA recommendation does this follow?
questions.explanation: Collecting outcome data is an AANA recommendation.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA mentors a high school student from an underrepresented group. Which AANA recommendation does this follow?
options: Encourage diverse students to consider nurse anesthesiology
Collect health outcomes data by race and ethnicity
Maintain anti-racist policies at the facility level
questions.explanation: Encouraging diverse students is an AANA recommendation.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA uses a standardized PONV prophylaxis protocol for all patients to reduce variation. Which AANA recommendation does this follow?
options: Collect outcomes data for quality review
questions.explanation: Evidence-based protocols reduce unwarranted variation.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA considers local community health needs when planning outreach. Which AANA recommendation applies?
questions.explanation: Awareness of community needs is an AANA recommendation.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A competent adult refuses a regional block despite clear benefits. What should the CRNA do?
options: Respect the refusal and offer alternatives
Place the block after sedation anyway
Decline to provide anesthesia for the case
Ask the surgeon to consent for the patient
questions.explanation: Autonomy requires respecting an informed refusal.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA advocates for extra monitoring for a high-risk patient despite pushback about cost. Which pillar is primarily reflected?
questions.explanation: Preventing harm reflects non-maleficence.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA provides the same PONV prophylaxis to all patients regardless of insurance. Which pillar is reflected?
questions.explanation: Equal and equitable treatment reflects justice.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA declines to perform a block in a patient with infection at the site. Which pillar is reflected?
questions.explanation: Avoiding harm reflects non-maleficence.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient asks for a nerve block to reduce opioids; the CRNA explains risks and benefits and places it. Which pillars are MOST involved?
questions.explanation: The patient's informed choice (autonomy) and benefit (beneficence) are central.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient with limited English is consented using a hospital interpreter. Which ethical principle is supported?
questions.explanation: Proper consent supports autonomy.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient is consented after receiving a large dose of sedative and cannot recall the discussion. What is the problem?
options: Consent may not be valid due to impaired capacity
Consent is valid once the form is signed
The surgeon's consent already covers anesthesia
questions.explanation: Consent must be informed and voluntary; impaired capacity threatens validity.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A surgeon asks the CRNA to skip explaining anesthesia risks to save time. What should the CRNA do?
options: Accept the surgeon's consent as covering anesthesia
Let the patient sign without an explanation of risks
questions.explanation: Anesthesia consent is separate and must meet all requirements.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient declines blood products for religious reasons. What does patient-centered care require?
options: Respect the patient's values and plan accordingly
Give blood if needed despite refusal
Refuse to provide anesthesia without blood consent
Ask the surgeon to override the decision
questions.explanation: Patient-centered care respects preferences and values.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA arranges a follow-up call with a patient after an awareness event. Which dimension of patient-centered care is reflected?
questions.explanation: Emotional support is a key dimension.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient's family is included in the preop discussion with permission. Which dimension is reflected?
options: Access to care through scheduling support
questions.explanation: Including family is a dimension of patient-centered care.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient's anesthesia plan is coordinated with cardiology and nephrology. Which dimension is reflected?
options: Emotional support during the perioperative period
questions.explanation: Coordination of care involves multidisciplinary planning.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient has transportation issues, and the team schedules telehealth preop. Which dimension is reflected?
questions.explanation: Access to care is a dimension of patient-centered care.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient is transferred to ICU with a detailed anesthesia handoff. Which dimension is reflected?
questions.explanation: Continuity and transition focuses on handoffs.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA respects a patient's request to keep her head covered for religious reasons. Which dimension is reflected?
options: Access to care through flexible scheduling
questions.explanation: Respecting values is a patient-centered dimension.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA uses teach-back to confirm understanding of postop instructions. Which dimension is reflected?
options: Access to care through scheduling support
